summary: In a fiction excerpt from Book 15, Emma prepares to leave the house with Ray Marlowe after an icy exchange with Amah, the family's stern elderly matriarch. Amah tells Ray that the Whistons' ways are old and demand respect, and that she measures people by outdated standards. Emma says Ray only wants to take her to lunch, and Ray, reluctant to cause Emma trouble, smiles and agrees. Amah's hostile stare and Ray's sardonic inner commentary give the scene a tense, uneasy tone.
one_line: Emma leaves for lunch with Ray Marlowe under the hostile, disapproving gaze of the old matriarch Amah in a Book 15 excerpt.
key_facts: Amah tells Ray Marlowe that the ways of the Whistons are old and strange to some, and that she measures by standards no longer in fashion.
Amah says, "Times change, Mr. Marlowe. Standards change. But the Whistons do not."
Amah tells Ray that what is demanded of those who would flutter near the family's flame is respect.
Amah says Ray must have the fortitude to endure if he wants to come to see the truth of this.
Emma intervenes by saying, "Ray just wants to take me to lunch."
Amah asks Ray, "Is that what you want, Mr. Marlowe?" and Ray replies, "If you don't mind."
Amah responds "None of my business" after Ray agrees to the lunch.
Emma tells Amah that the children have been fed and that Leela is putting the younger ones down for their nap.
Emma mentions a vegan guest named Veronica, and tells Amah she should be back in time for the children's afternoon lessons.
Ray has previously forced Emma to bear the weight of his conflicting interests once, and he does not want to do so again.
Ray's inner thoughts describe Amah's gaze as an accusation of rape, which he finds unfair given that the sexual aggression is only impending.
Ray reflects that he is starting to remember why it always seemed easier to pay for sex than to pursue Air Force women.
